_comment_overview: Decision-matrix frame, Stage 1 (2026-09-02). Additive config for modules/decision_frame.py's three-layer recommendation frame (evidence -> candidates -> scoring), separate from and parallel to the existing 39-rule engine in config/recommendations.json (unchanged). Tier B/C throughout (signal/data engineering + UI scoring plumbing, not a vehicle-dynamics method) -- every numeric entry below states its provenance grade so the write-up never presents a placeholder as a validated result. Design (three layers, provenance-grade scheme, Stage 1 scope = exit-oversteer scenario only) is fixed per the work order; this file does not redesign it.

intervention_evidence._comment: Stage 2 (Frame-Stage-2 Phase 3c, 2026-09-04) wired ABS/TC behind ONE global flag, default off. Deepening Phase 4c (2026-09-18, user decision) SPLITS this into per-source flags: ABS defaults ON now that Phase 3 resolved the trusted position channel (log_abs_pos) and this is treated as reviewed-enough to ship; TC/EB stay dormant pending their own channel-identity mapping (Frame-Stage-2 Phase 2's own UNCLEAR/READ-AND-RECORD findings, still unresolved). Confidence for the ABS bridges is explicitly 0.8, not 1.0 -- Stage 2's own autonomous 1.0 default is SUPERSEDED by this user decision, derived_from 'sensor boolean, single-session semantics, revisit' (a deliberately conservative confidence pending validation on more sessions, not a claim of full certainty).

abs.confidence_derived_from: Deepening Phase 4c (2026-09-18), user decision -- 'sensor boolean, single-session semantics, revisit'. Supersedes Stage 2's own autonomous confidence=1.0 default for this same evidence.

abs_inactive_corroborates_braking_instab._comment: User rule, verbatim: 'instability/locking under braking + ABS not intervening -> ABS map up'. Fires when abs_active reads 0 for the ENTIRE entry_1_brake phase window of a lap instance (never on a partial window -- 'inactive' means never fired, not merely low duty-cycle) AND that same corner shows unstable_yaw matrix-verdict evidence on entry_1_brake (the INST-BRK-* matrix cells' own verdict). The evidence's own source string reports the CURRENT log_abs_pos map position (Phase 3's trusted channel) for traceability -- not used to change the firing logic itself (no validated per-position 'more/less aggressive' ordering exists to route on, abs_position's own registry entry is explicitly non-monotonic). Corroborating evidence only -- adds to a candidate's evidence_refs (MIN-confidence rule), never generates a standalone action of its own.

abs_heavy_masks_verdict._comment: NEW, Deepening Phase 4c. User rule, verbatim: 'ABS regulating heavily through braking zones -> flag as masking, prefer brake-balance/platform levers'. Fires when abs_active's own duty cycle within a lap instance's entry_1_brake window exceeds heavy_duty_cycle_threshold. Distinct from the corroborating bridge above -- this is a MASKING FLAG, not evidence for a specific verdict: heavy ABS intervention means the corner's own CS_ratio/verdict reading at that phase may reflect the ABS system's own regulation rather than the car's raw mechanical balance, so brake-balance/platform-tuning candidates (brake_balance_signature's own plausibility check, ride_height/spring levers) should be preferred over a literal reading of the braking-phase verdict. Implemented as a flag attached to matching evidence (masked_by_heavy_abs=True), not a new evidence type of its own -- modules/decision_frame.py's own candidate/scoring layers read it to avoid over-trusting a masked verdict, never to invent a new action.
abs_heavy_masks_verdict.heavy_duty_cycle_threshold_derived_from: ROUND number, NOT gap-selected -- only 5 real per-instance ABS duty-cycle observations exist on GT3_PRC_MLA-v3.txt (range 26%-57%, too few for a robust gap), Deepening Phase 4c census. 0.5 (more than half the braking phase under ABS regulation) is deliberately conservative/rare -- only 1 of the 5 observed instances would qualify -- revisit once more sessions provide a real distribution to gap-select against.

tc.confidence_note: Unchanged from Stage 2 -- TC stays dormant (Deepening Phase 4c, user decision: 'TC/EB stay dormant pending mapping'), so this confidence value is not yet load-bearing either way.

tc_active_corroborates_traction_limited._comment: Fires when ecu_B_tc_act reads 1 anywhere inside a lap instance's exit_4/exit_5 phase window AND that corner/phase already carries oversteer matrix-verdict evidence. Corroborates the ls_disambiguation traction_limited classification (or, where LS_ratio itself is invalid/absent, stands as independent traction-limited evidence on its own) -- added to evidence_refs, never a standalone action.

plausibility_checks._comment: Cheap-first-tier checks (Phase 3: 'generated whenever their evidence fires, any scenario'). Both are Tier B: standard data-engineering checks against config-driven bounds, not a vehicle-dynamics claim.

tyre_pressure_window._comment: Per-axle hot-pressure plausibility window. NOT DERIVABLE from anything in this repo -- verified by search: config/channels.json, config/parameters.json, config/setup_parameters.json, config/car_data.json all contain zero tyre-pressure entries (only Brake Pressure Front/Rear channel labels, an unrelated signal). Left null on purpose rather than guessing a number for a real physical limit. Per-corner override is a later UI item (per-weekend, user-editable); Stage 1 reads these config defaults only.
tyre_pressure_window.derived_from: NEEDS USER INPUT -- no target hot-pressure window exists anywhere in this project's config or docs. Supply front/rear (or per-corner) min/max in psi from tyre data sheet or team practice before this check can ever fire; until then it is wired but permanently silent (no evidence, not a false negative).

brake_balance_signature._comment: Front axle beyond its own limit while rear stays healthy, during the braking phase -- a data-driven plausibility read, not a new vehicle-dynamics method. Deliberately expressed in terms of classify_fn's own severity labels (moderate/strong), not raw CS_ratio numbers, so this file never duplicates config/parameters.json's classification.STRONG_CSF/STRONG_CSR/MODERATE_CSF/MODERATE_CSR thresholds -- those are re-derived per estimator/car (CLAUDE.md deviation taxonomy) and duplicating their values here would risk drift the next time they change. No brake-balance/brake-bias signature logic existed anywhere in modules/ before this (verified by search) -- new Stage 1 evidence source.
brake_balance_signature.derived_from: Tier B. 'Beyond limit' = front axle's classify_fn severity on entry_1_brake reaches front_beyond_severity_min (today: 'moderate', i.e. CS_ratio_f at or past config/parameters.json classification.MODERATE_CSF). 'Healthy' = rear axle's severity on the same phase stays at/below rear_healthy_severity_max (today: 'normal', i.e. rear CS_ratio_r has not crossed even MODERATE_CSR). Reuses the existing _phase_verdict/classify_fn path (modules/recommendation.py) unmodified, per-axle -- guarantees this check can never disagree with what the stability grid already shows for the same corner/phase.

scoring_weights._comment: Every weight here is a project-lead-elicited PLACEHOLDER (Stage 1, 2026-09-02) -- neutral (1.0) except phase_importance's elicited exit>entry ordering, none tuned against real scored output yet. Stage 2 calibration item (see thesis_notes.md Stage 1 entry).

phase_importance._comment: User instruction (this session): exit phases weigh highest for laptime. Ordinal ordering is the real content (entry < turn-in < apex < exit); the specific magnitudes are placeholders pending Stage 2 calibration against real scored output.

effect_class_multiplier._comment: Added during Phase 4 (scoring layer) -- not anticipated by Phase 1's own spec text, needed to turn the candidate layer's categorical effect_class ('primary'/'secondary', see modules/decision_frame.py generate_candidates) into a numeric score component. Placeholder, same status as every other weight here.

scoring_weights.effort_weight_note: Applied INVERSELY at score time (Phase 4 owns the exact formula): a cheap change (cockpit/seconds) should score higher than an equally-effective expensive one (garage/hours), all else equal.
scoring_weights.derived_from: project-lead-elicited placeholders, decision-frame Stage 1 package (2026-09-02) -- see thesis_notes.md for the elicitation context and the Stage 2 calibration item this leaves open.

driver_feedback_weighting._comment: Deepening Phase 4d (2026-09-18). NEW evidence dimension -- Stage 1/2 had no driver-feedback axis at all (explicitly flagged as a Stage 2 open item in the original Stage 1 close-out). A driver_feedback evidence item's own CONFIDENCE (not a new action, not a new candidate -- it is attached to an EXISTING candidate's evidence_refs when its own verdict/corner/phase agrees, via the same MIN-confidence rule every other corroborating evidence source already uses) ramps LINEARLY from confidence_floor at |raw feedback|=1 to 1.0 at full_confidence_at_raw_abs.
driver_feedback_weighting.derived_from: User decision (this session, quoted verbatim in the work order): 'counts from 1, very little weight'. full_confidence_at_raw_abs=4 is NOT a new number invented for this curve -- it is the SAME |4| threshold config/recommendations.json settings.consistency_gate.feedback_override.feedback_override_raw_min already uses for 'approaching undrivable' (the scale's own established confirmation floor, modules/recommendation.py VERDICT_EXPECTED_FEEDBACK_SIGN/_override_direction_ok), reused rather than a second, disagreeing anchor. confidence_floor=0.1 is a round, deliberately small placeholder for 'very little weight' at the scale's own bottom (|1|='barely noticeable' per the feedback-table's own caption) -- not gap-selected against any data (driver feedback confidence has no real-data distribution to gap-select against yet), a Stage-2-style calibration item like every other scoring weight in this file.

ls_threshold_evidence._comment: LS THRESHOLD DECISION (2026-09-20, user + reviewer, resolving PLAN.md PARKED 'LS_ratio threshold proposal'): thresholds ship PHASE-SCOPED, not flat, and live HERE (frame-evidence config), not in config/parameters.json's classification block -- deliberately, so they can never become a classification/severity-colour verdict tier the way STRONG_CSF/CSR are. modules/decision_frame.py's own _build_ls_threshold_evidence consumes this block. Full derivation: thesis_notes.md 'LS-evidence work package: negative-population co-occurrence census' (71 negative worst-phase instances, both real sessions, censused against brake/throttle/ABS/TC/|ax|/repeatability) and its own PLAN.md PARKED verdict entry.
ls_threshold_evidence.STRONG_LSF_derived_from: LS-evidence census pooled p10 (front), same physical anchor logic as CS_ratio's own STRONG_CSF/CSR (0 = the ratio's own peak-force point, minus a data-sized margin) -- Metrology extension Phase 2's own repaired-estimator distribution, n=31 pooled corners. Reopen condition: a validity-repair-scale re-derivation if a third session's own distribution shifts this materially; small-n caveat carried over unchanged from the original proposal.
ls_threshold_evidence.STRONG_LSR_derived_from: Same population/method as STRONG_LSF, rear axle pooled p10. Reopen condition identical.
ls_threshold_evidence.exit_phase_confidence_discount_derived_f: LS-evidence census, 2026-09-20: exit-phase negative instances corroborate at only 34% (15/44) vs braking 89% (8/9) and turn-in/apex 72% (13/18) -- the discriminating factor is NAMED, not just observed: TC (the natural exit/traction corroborator) fires on only 3 samples in v3's entire session (0.0044%, thesis_notes.md 'Frame-Stage-2 Phase 2: intervention-channel survey'), so exit-phase readings are structurally unable to be TC-corroborated this session regardless of whether the underlying signal is real -- an evidence gap, not a demonstrated absence of signal. 0.5 reuses intervention_evidence.abs.confidence's own 0.8-cap PRECEDENT (a MIN-confidence ceiling, not a new discount mechanism) at a value matching this source's own weaker (34%, vs ABS's 41.92% co-occurrence) corroboration rate. Applied via min() against the SAME repeat-fraction confidence _build_corner_verdict_evidence already computes -- repeatability across a corner's own laps (the Dubai C3 pattern: exit_5 rear, repeat=4/4, corroborated via repeatability alone with zero TC activity) is what lifts a reading UP TO this ceiling rather than leaving it at a low one-off fraction; min() cannot inflate a genuinely low fraction past what it already is. REOPEN CONDITION, stated explicitly per the work order: a session with real, non-trivial TC activity re-derives this discount (or removes the need for it) by closing the evidence gap directly instead of working around it.

_comment_parameter_windows: One entry per config/setup_parameters.json registry key (46 keys, verified against that file directly -- not from memory). 'nominal' + 'span' sourced from that registry's own typical_window/value_space fields wherever a real team-typical value exists there. Deepening Phase 4a (2026-09-18): every remaining fillable null filled per the work order's own rule -- nominal = value_space range midpoint when no typical_window nominal exists, span = HALF the typical window's own full width when one exists (matching this file's own pre-existing convention exactly: arb_fl nominal=4/span=1 from typical_window{min:3,max:5}, i.e. span is the ONE-SIDED half-width, not the full window), else HALF the parameter's own full legal value_space range as a generous fallback span when no typical_window exists at all (flagged as wider/weaker than a real team-typical span, never presented as one). Still null+flagged where genuinely unfillable -- a plain enum-index midpoint with no underlying numeric quantity is not filled (CLAUDE.md 'never invent'; see arb_front_mount/wing_position notes below for the two cases and why they differ). Used by Phase 4's settings-window-distance component (current setup value vs this window; a null window, or a non-numeric current value, makes that component neutral for the parameter -- modules/decision_frame.py's own _settings_window_component now catches the latter defensively too, a real latent-crash fix found while filling this section, see thesis_notes.md).

_comment_interaction_table: Stage 1 (2026-09-02) seeded only two lever families (rear ARB, diff_position) plus a user-elicited camber pairing. Deepening Phase 4b (2026-09-18) extended this to EVERY extractable cross-reference in the 39-rule matrix: systematically walked every (parameter, direction) pair that appears as a suggestion anywhere in config/recommendations.json (39 rules, all statuses) and, for each, checked whether ANY OTHER rule uses the SAME parameter -- same direction for a DIFFERENT axis (a genuine same-direction side-benefit, sign=+1) or the OPPOSITE direction for a DIFFERENT axis (this candidate's own direction trades that other axis's margin away, sign=-1). Covers arb_fl/fr/rl/rr, camber_fl/fr (matrix-derived, alongside the existing user-elicited braking/traction entries -- both coexist, not a duplicate), diff_position, ride_height_front/rear, tc_lon, toe_front -- all grade 'derived-from-matrix'. NOT extracted (deliberately, reasons vary): abs_position (categorical/non-monotonic, a signed axis relationship would misrepresent it); tc_lat and the 20 damper channels (each used by only ONE rule in the matrix, no opposite-direction cross-reference exists to extract); front_arb/rear_arb (dead WP2-placeholder names used only by the 7 retired seed rules, not real setup_parameters.json keys, never produced as a real candidate action); wing_position (increase is used to fix BOTH understeer, matrix_us_brk_high, braking phase, AND oversteer, matrix_os_tin_high/matrix_os_exit_high, turn-in/exit phases -- genuinely phase-dependent and non-monotonic in the matrix itself, a single signed entry would misrepresent that, left uncovered rather than forced). springs_front/rear got the work order's own literature-anchored PROPOSED entries instead (Segers ch.9 pp.199ff/ch.10 pp.221-256) -- the ONE registry parameter pair with ZERO matrix cross-reference at all (verified: appears in none of the 39 rules), exactly the gap those two literature-anchored principles (front/rear roll-stiffness distribution shifts balance; spring-rate change also touches ride/aero-platform, unlike ARB) were given to fill. The THIRD literature point the work order named -- lateral weight transfer TOTAL is geometry/CoG-fixed, only the front/rear DISTRIBUTION is tunable -- is not a table row (there is no 'total_grip' axis in this vocabulary to attach it to): it is the reason EVERY ARB/spring entry above targets a balance axis (understeer_tendency/oversteer_tendency) and none targets anything resembling total grip, stated here rather than as an unused row. Every other registry parameter x axis pair remains implicitly null/uncovered -- not written out as thousands of explicit null entries. grade is exactly 'derived-from-matrix', 'proposed', or 'proposed (Segers ch.9/10)' (a literature-anchored proposed entry, still advisory-capped like any other 'proposed' grade -- the citation names WHY it is credible, not a higher trust tier).
_comment_performance_axes: Fixed vocabulary for performance_axis below, referenced by Phase 4's interaction-penalty lookup: understeer_tendency, oversteer_tendency (kept as two separate axes, not one bipolar scale, so a signed entry always reads as 'helps/hurts THIS named tendency' unambiguously), yaw_stability, braking_performance, traction_performance, platform_stability (added Deepening Phase 4b, 2026-09-18, for the springs-vs-ARB aero-platform distinction -- Segers ch.9/10). Phase-agnostic on purpose -- Phase 4 matches an entry's axis against the VERDICT TYPE of the evidence's other active problems at that corner (already phase+corner+verdict scoped), not against the axis name itself. braking_performance/traction_performance/platform_stability are all currently STRUCTURALLY INERT in modules/decision_frame.py's own _AXIS_TO_VERDICT (no mapping to a real verdict type exists for any of the three, so their entries are documented provenance, never an active scoring contribution, until a matching evidence source exists) -- understeer_tendency/oversteer_tendency/yaw_stability are the only three that fire today. Extend this list only when a new interaction entry needs an axis not already here.

Rule status is 'retired'/superseded-by-matrix but the recorded mechanism is real, not invented for this table -- positive side-effect on yaw stability from the same rear-ARB-soften lever this candidate's primary effect (exit oversteer/traction) already uses.

Increasing diff_position for this candidate's own primary purpose (exit oversteer, traction-limited branch) therefore carries a negative side-effect on understeer wherever else it is present -- opposite-direction cross-reference between these two matrix cells.

_comment_conditions: FRAME DEPTH PROGRAMME Step 1 (2026-09-22, PLAN.md 'FRAME DEPTH PROGRAMME', reviewer-approved fixed design). Adds an optional per-lever_bridges-entry 'conditions' list (schema: each item is {type: evidence_corroboration|setup_state|phase_transient, required: bool, ...type-specific fields}) so a candidate's confidence can depend on MORE than the single matrix_verdict evidence item that fires it -- corroborating evidence (e.g. lockup, damper motion) and the CURRENT setup state (a lever already at its window edge), not just the verdict pattern. Deliberately excludes any cross-lap repeat/consistency requirement, per the 2026-09-22 candidate-census finding (thesis_notes.md 'Frame candidate census: single-lap evidence confirmed on both real sessions'): every corner_verdict/matrix_verdict evidence item on both real sessions rests on exactly 1 repeating lap, so a repeat-count condition would suppress 100% of candidates on both sessions -- repeatability stays the EXISTING confidence discount's own job (repeat_fraction x valid_fraction, already computed per evidence item), never re-litigated as a second, stricter gate here. evaluate_conditions() (modules/decision_frame.py) returns one of PASS (every condition evaluable and passing -- confidence untouched) / SUPPRESS (a REQUIRED condition evaluable and failing -- candidate not emitted at all) / CAP_ADVISORY (a non-required condition failing, OR ANY condition not-evaluable for any reason -- missing evidence source this run, unfilled setup sheet, missing registry window -- applies not_evaluable_confidence_cap below via the EXISTING min()-confidence machinery, no new formula). 'CAP_ADVISORY, never SUPPRESS, for an evidence gap' is the load-bearing distinction: a condition this frame simply CANNOT check (no signal, not corroborated one way or the other) is not the same claim as a condition that was checked and found false -- 'cannot corroborate' is not 'contradicted', so it degrades confidence rather than deleting the candidate, the same honesty posture build_evidence's own docstring states project-wide ('an honest [], never a fabricated fallback').

conditions.not_evaluable_confidence_cap_derived_fro: Reuses ls_threshold_evidence.exit_phase_confidence_discount's own 0.5 PRECEDENT (2026-09-20) -- not a new number invented for this mechanism. Same justification transfers directly: an evidence gap (there, exit-phase TC corroboration being structurally unavailable this session; here, any not-evaluable condition -- missing evidence source, unfilled setup sheet, missing registry window) caps confidence via min() rather than suppressing the candidate outright, at a value already established in this same config file for exactly this kind of gap. Applied via the SAME min()-confidence mechanism every other cap in this file uses (MARGINAL-verdict cap, exit-phase LS discount, ABS-masking) -- min() can only ever LOWER a candidate's confidence, never raise it, so a candidate whose OWN evidence already reports confidence below 0.5 is untouched (never inflated up to the cap).

_comment_damper_motion: FRAME DEPTH PROGRAMME Step 2 (2026-09-22, modules/damper_motion.py). Per-corner, per-TRANSIENT-phase (entry/exit only, never apex -- Segers ch.11 boundary condition, docs/segers_bridge_review.md C11-1) loading/unloading classification from log_susp_travel_* -- the evidence source Step 1's evidence_corroboration condition type was built to consume, no consumer wired to it yet (that is Step 3's own job). Two real-data findings, thesis_notes.md 'Damper motion sign-convention and threshold derivation' entry: (1) SIGN CONVENTION, empirically checked on BOTH real sessions (corr(front-axle travel, braking ax): Dubai +0.4905, v3 +0.2025, both POSITIVE and agreeing) -- travel DECREASES as braking gets harder, and harder braking physically compresses the front axle, so DECREASING travel = compression = loading, INCREASING = extension = unloading (the OPPOSITE of the first, unverified guess this package started with -- exactly why the work order required checking, not assuming). (2) THRESHOLD DERIVATION: apex_3 was the originally planned 'near-zero reference' population but both sessions' own apex_3 phase segments are too narrow for this project's own phase segmentation (zero >=2-sample rate windows on either session) -- reused this project's own EXISTING straight-line mask precedent (|ax|<0.5, |ay|<0.5 g, the same mask the Fz-integration/aero work already established as its own 'nothing dynamic happening' convention) as the reference population instead.

damper_motion.rate_threshold_mm_s_derived_from: Pooled straight-line (|ax|<0.5,|ay|<0.5 g, kerb-excluded) |travel rate| median across both real sessions and all non-dead wheels: 0.975 mm/s (n=1830, Dubai 510 windows p50=0.825, v3 1320 windows p50=1.061) -- rounded to a clean 1.0 mm/s just above it. This is NOT a clean bimodal gap (the straight-line population's own upper tail, p90=4.67/p95=6.68 mm/s, genuinely overlaps the transient population's own median, 1.87 mm/s pooled -- real road-texture/engine-vibration chassis motion exists even on a straight, this is not pure sensor noise) -- the median of the 'nothing deliberately dynamic happening' reference population is the honest, data-grounded choice available, not a cleanly-separated threshold; revisit if a future session's own distribution suggests otherwise. diagnostics/inspect_damper_motion_sign_and_threshold.py, thesis_notes.md.
damper_motion.min_valid_fraction_derived_from: Pooled transient-phase window valid_fraction (non-kerb-masked, finite samples / window length) across both real sessions: p5=0.712, p10=0.783, p25=0.934, p50~1.0 (n=1258) -- most windows are nearly fully valid, only a small tail is meaningfully kerb-degraded. 0.7 sits just below p5, flagging roughly the bottom 5% sparsest windows as not-evaluable without discarding the typical (>=0.78, ~90% of) window. diagnostics/inspect_damper_motion_sign_and_threshold.py, thesis_notes.md.
